items.name: Brood heart-crystal
items.description: A fist of white crystal from the heart of a salted Weave-Eater. It hums against your palm.

items.name: Calcified shard
items.description: White crystal left where a Weave-Eater stood, salt-bound and still.

items.name: Salt-cask
items.description: A small sealed cask of Ash-Walker salt, marked with a harpoon.

items.name: Petrified bone
items.description: Grey bone turned to stone. The Eaters won't touch it.

items.name: Salt of the First Sea
items.description: A sack of white salt, tied with three knots by Mother Vane. It is heavier than salt should be.

items.name: Ash-Walker salt-pouch
items.description: A hunter's salt-pouch of grey hide, tied with amber cord in one family's own knot. A cultist wore it on his belt like a purse.

items.name: Kesh's harpoon
items.description: Petrified leviathan bone, too old to burn, with a barb that was never quite straight. The amber cord has been cut away.

items.name: Violet grit
items.description: A pinch of the grey a Hollow Man leaves, with violet grains in it that catch the light. It is cold, and stays cold in your hand.

items.name: Pot of tear-daub
items.description: A clay pot no bigger than an egg, crusted purple at the rim, with a thumbprint pressed into the daub.

documents.title: The Tear-Marked Litany
documents.text:
Kneel in the ash, for the ash is honest.
The Weave was a lie told by the Makers, and the grey is the truth coming home.
Wear the bone, that the Kings may know you for theirs.
Mark the tear, that the Kings may find you in the dark.
The eternal Void hungers for the light.
Give it the light.

(In the margin, another hand: 'Salt from the Ridge caves, three casks. The Patriarch says: no salt, no binding. Let them see what walks when there is no salt.')
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: 'The eternal Void hungers for the light' is the cult's cry in book1 ch.10; the Patriarch of Ash (Torvyn Embercloak) is canon, and the purple tear and preparing for the Kings belong to the later House of Ash (series_bible.md). The rest of the litany is GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: Salt of the First Sea
documents.text:
Mother Vane's words over the salt, as she taught them to you:

Salt of the First Sea!
By the Maker's hand!
By the Keeper's breath!
I bind the Chaos!
I seal the Wound!

'Say it loud. The salt doesn't hear you. You hear you. A binding done quiet is a binding done by half.'

'Salt binds. It does not unmake. Remember that, townsman, when you're tempted to think a thing is finished.'
documents.canonStatus: The chant is CANON (book1 ch.20); Mother Vane's advice is GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: Ash in the Bread
documents.text:
To my mother at Cinderfold, if anyone is left there to read it:

Vorn says the ash is honest. He says the grey is the truth coming home and we should kneel in it. I knelt. I wore the bone.
Then we went through Cinderfold after the grey had, to see what the truth looked like. The bread was still on the table, Mam. Ash all through, the shape of bread and nothing in it.
I'm going. The coin is what I had off the offering-bowl. Salt from the Ridge caves is dearer than bone, and I mean to buy some.
Don't wait up.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Cult of Ash, its bone masks and Vorn are CANON (book1 ch.10, world_bible.md); the letter and its writer are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Waybook at Wain's Rest
documents.text:
Wain's Rest, on the salt road. Wains and travellers, as they come.

Six wains west with salt from the old pans, for the Peaks road. Ate the mutton. Complained of the mutton.
Four wains. Carter Hobb says the pans are crusting grey at the far edge. Says it the way you'd say rain.
Two wains, one driver. He would not stop for his supper. Said the water tastes of copper now, and so it does.
No wains.
No wains. Grey on the south fields this morning. By noon it was at the hedge.
The orchard-men have gone up the north road to Oakhaven with what they could carry. Hollin asked me to come. I said the book wants keeping.
No wains. The road is quiet at night in a way I don't like. Not quiet like sleeping. Quiet like listening.

(Pressed hard into the foot of the page, in the same hand:) If you are reading this, you came by the road, so the road is still there. Go back the way you came.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Wain's Rest, its waybook, the salt road and its people. The copper taste of the grey's dust is CANON (book1 ch.20); the Wasting creeping on is CANON (world_bible.md).

documents.title: The Deacon's Tally
documents.text:
Given to the light at the pit, this moon, that the Kings may know us ready.

Ridge salt, two casks. It would not burn. Buried it, deep.
A wain-horse off the salt road. Old. It went quietly.
The last rafters of Wain's Rest, for the fire.
A hound that came too near the pit. It did not mean to be given. Few do.
One Ash-Walker, young, taken on the knoll. Given on the third night.
He would not kneel. He would not say the words. He said his aunt would come for him, and said it again, and then he said nothing.
His harpoon would not burn. I keep it. A thing the light refuses is a thing to be studied.

The eternal Void hungers for the light. Feed it.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: 'The eternal Void hungers for the light' is the cult's cry (book1 ch.10), and preparing for the Kings belongs to the later House of Ash (series_bible.md), used early as in the Litany; the Ash-Deacon, his tally and Kesh are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: How a Salt Line Is Laid
documents.text:
Scratched on a slab of petrified bark and left at the gap in the Ridge, where the line is laid:

Salt of the First Sea is not thrown. It is walked. One hand low, the grains falling in a thread, the feet never crossing the thread once it is down. Sing the chant under the breath, not aloud: the grey has no ears, but the Eaters do.

The line holds a season if the wind is kind, a month if it is not. It is laid again by whoever is Salt-Speaker, alone, at dusk. Nobody watches her lay it. That is not a rule. It is manners.

Past the line the ash goes on a little way and then it doesn't. Do not step past the line to see. You have been told what is there. Believe it, and keep your thread.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Ash-Walkers binding Weave-Eaters with Salt of the First Sea and the chant are CANON (book1 ch.20); the laying of a line, the slab and its rules are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Faceless One
documents.text:
A page in Chieftain Grohl's square hand, left at the foot of the standing stone by the grey:

Third watch at the Statue. It does not move. I have said this before. I say it again because the ash round its feet is further from it every dawn, as if it had stepped back in the night and stepped forward again before I woke. It has no face. I have begun to think it had one once and gave it up, the way we give our dead to the old sea.

The Walkers before my grandfather said the faceless stones were set up by the Weave itself, to mark where it had been mended and would not be mended again. The cult say they are the Void's own teeth. I say a thing that stands still at the edge of the grey for a hundred years is doing something, and I will know what before I am given to the sea.

Last-light grows at its feet. I did not pick it.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Statues, faceless monoliths in the Wasting, are CANON (world_bible.md), and so are the Ash-Walkers and the Cult of Ash (book1 ch.10, ch.20); Grohl's watch and this page are GAME-ONLY.

quests.title: Salt Is Not Given
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Weave-Eaters, salt that turns them to white crystal, Chieftain Grohl and Mother Vane are canon (book1 ch.20); the Unwoven Flats and this trial are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Hunt Weave-Eaters on the Unwoven Flats with Ash-Walker salt, and come back alive to Chieftain Grohl.
quests.offer:
"The salt is earned on the flats." Mother Vane closes your hand around a pouch of white salt. It is heavier than it should be. "Weave-Eaters feed on the Unwoven Flats, west of the Ridge. They're hunger, walking. A blade goes through them and breaks."

"So you don't cut first. You salt, and then you break. Five of them. Grohl will want to see you come back. Most don't."
quests.complete: Chieftain Grohl looks you over with his one eye: the grey dust on your boots, the white crystal caught in your coat. "Five. And you came back." He grunts. "You fight like a townsman. But you came back. Vane! This one can stay."

steps.text: Salt and shatter Weave-Eaters on the Unwoven Flats.

quests.title: The Tear-Marked Shrine
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Cult of Ash (Torvyn Embercloak, Vorn) and its iron-wired bone masks are canon (book1 ch.10, series_bible.md); the purple tear is the later House of Ash's symbol (series_bible.md), used early here; the shrine on the Ashland Rim is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Break the bone-masked cultists at the Cult of Ash shrine in the south-west and topple their shrine. They have been stealing the Ash-Walkers' salt.
quests.offer:
"You want salt for a well. Then help me keep it." Grohl drives the butt of his mace into the ash. "Bone-masks. The Cult of Ash. They pray to the grey like it's a god, and they daub a purple tear on everything they touch."

"They have a shrine in the south-west, at the end of the old waste road. They steal our salt so we can't hold the Eaters off, and they call it a sacrament. Break the masks. Six will teach the rest some distance. Then pull their shrine down."
quests.complete: Grohl reads the litany slowly, lips moving, then crushes it in his fist. "'The Void hungers.' Aye. So do I." He throws the ball of vellum into the fire. "Good work. Vane will want to see you."

steps.text: Break the bone-masked cultists at the shrine.
Topple the purple-tear shrine.

objectives.say: The shrine comes down in a spill of wired bone. Under the altar-stone is a scrap of vellum in a close, careful hand.

quests.title: Heart of the Brood
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Salt of the First Sea and its binding words are canon (book1 ch.20); feeding the salt with a brood-heart is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Destroy the Weave-Eater brood at the Wasting's edge and bring its heart-crystal to Mother Vane, so the salt is strong enough to bind a seed. The brood is dangerous alone.
quests.offer:
"Salt for a cooking pot, I'd give you now. Salt for a seed must be fed." Mother Vane opens a cask and shows you salt gone faintly grey. "It has to taste the thing it binds. There's a brood of Eaters at the Wasting's edge, south along the Ridge. Great ones, fat on what they've unmade."

"Kill the brood. When the salt takes them, what's left at the heart is a crystal, white and humming. Bring me that, and I'll wake the salt with it."
quests.complete: "There." Mother Vane's hands shake, just a little. "Salt of the First Sea. It'll bind your seed. Bind it, mind. Whoever planted it can still wake it, if they come with will enough. Salt buys time. It doesn't buy the world."

steps.text: Destroy the Weave-Eater brood at the Wasting's edge and take its heart-crystal.
Bring the heart-crystal to Mother Vane.

objectives.text: Give the heart-crystal to Mother Vane
objectives.say: She drops the crystal into the cask. The grey salt flares white all at once, and the cave is as bright as noon.

quests.title: Salt for the Well
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Void-Seed in Oakhaven's water is canon (book1 ch.4); binding it with salt is GAME-ONLY. Oakhaven's later erasure stays canon: the salt only makes the seed wait.
quests.summary: Carry the Salt of the First Sea home by the dangerous north road, salt Oakhaven's Communal Well, and give what is left to Corwin Ashby.
quests.offer:
Mother Vane ties the sack herself, three knots, and puts it in your arms. "The north road runs to your village from here, if you're brave or a fool. Most things on it will be glad to see you."

"Pour it into the well and say the words. Then give what's left to your elder and tell him to salt the stones again every new moon. It won't stop what's coming. It will make it wait."
quests.complete:
Corwin listens to all of it: the toll-book, the Seeker's warrant, the road to Argentis. He doesn't interrupt.

"So Wren and the soldier's boy are beyond us. For now." He sets the salt by his door, where he'll see it every day. "And the thing in our well sleeps, and we keep it sleeping. Every new moon." He looks at you a long while. "You went to the edge of the world for a well and a boy you've never met. Oakhaven won't forget it, whatever comes."

steps.text: Take the north road home to Oakhaven and salt the Communal Well.

objectives.say: You pour the salt into the well and say the words aloud. Something far down in the dark water flinches. The faint violet at the bottom of the shaft dims to nothing, and for the first time in weeks the water smells only of water.

steps.text: Give the rest of the salt to Corwin Ashby.

objectives.text: Give the salt to Corwin Ashby
objectives.say: "Salt. From the Ash-Walkers?" Corwin weighs the sack in both hands. "I thought they were a story we told children."

quests.title: Hounds on the Harpoon-Line
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (ash hounds)
quests.summary: Kill six ash hounds hunting in the dead snags west of the enclave.
quests.offer: "Ash hounds. Wolves, once, before the grey got into them. Now they're wolves that don't need to eat, and eat anyway." He spits into the ash. "They've been at our harpoon-line in the western snags. Six. Bring me nothing back; I'll believe you."
quests.complete: "Good. The line holds another night." From Grohl, that is a speech.

steps.text: Kill the ash hounds in the western snags.

quests.title: White Shards
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: salted Weave-Eaters turning to white crystal is canon (book1 ch.20); using the shards is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Gather six calcified shards from the Weave-Eaters you salt and shatter.
quests.offer: "When the salt takes an Eater it leaves white crystal. Most of my people kick it into the ash." She holds a shard up to the firelight. "Wasteful. Ground fine, it sweetens the salt. Bring me six shards. Whole ones."
quests.complete: "Whole. Good hands." She drops them one by one into a stone bowl, and each rings like a small bell.

steps.text: Gather calcified shards from salted Weave-Eaters.

quests.title: Leviathan Bone
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Ash-Walker harpoons of petrified leviathan bone and a petrified ribcage on the ash plain are canon images (book1 ch.20); this ribcage and the quest are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Chip five pieces of petrified bone from the old ribcage in the south for Oska's harpoons.
quests.offer:
Oska doesn't look up from the harpoon she is carving. "The Eaters won't eat old bone. Nobody knows why. So we make our harpoons of it."

"There's a ribcage in the south, big as a hall, from something that swam when the ash was sea, or so the old ones say. Chip me five good pieces. Hard ones. The soft ones splinter."
quests.complete: She taps each piece against her teeth, listening, and keeps four. "Good enough. The fifth I'll make you a luck-charm of. You'll want luck."

steps.text: Chip petrified bone from the old ribcage.

quests.title: The Stolen Casks
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: Take back three salt-casks the Cult of Ash carried off to their shrine in the south-west.
quests.offer:
"Three casks." The salt-trader counts on her fingers as if she might have got it wrong. "Three casks of good salt gone in one night, and the tracks go south-west to the bone-masks' shrine. They don't eat it. They don't sell it. They just keep it from us."

"Bring them back and I'll trade you anything on my table at cost. Well. Near cost."
quests.complete: "All three, and the seals unbroken." Sefa rolls them behind her stall. "You're a better thief than they are."

steps.text: Take back the stolen salt-casks from the cult shrine.

quests.title: Cinderfold
quests.canonStatus: CANON creature (Hollow Men, book1 ch.4); Cinderfold is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Put down the Hollow Men in the ruins of Cinderfold, north-west of the enclave, and find the house with the carved fish.
quests.offer:
"I was born in Cinderfold, north of here, before the grey went through it. It didn't take the houses. It took everything that lived in them." She doesn't stop polishing her scales. "They walk the lanes now. Grey. Saying they're hungry."

"Put six of them down. And find the house with the fish carved over the door. I'd like to know it's still standing."
quests.complete: "The fish." Sefa smiles, just barely. "My father carved that. He couldn't carve."

steps.text: Put down the Hollow Men of Cinderfold and find the Brine house.

objectives.text: Find the house with the carved fish
objectives.say: The door is grey like everything else, but the carved fish over the lintel is still there. Inside: a child's cup, grey as the ash.

quests.title: The Old Salt Road
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Ash-Walkers and Salt of the First Sea (book1 ch.20), the Verdant Shore, the Ridge of Long Shadows and the Veridian Keepers (book3 ch.1-2) are CANON; that the Ash-Walkers' first salt came from the western shore, the old road over the mountains and Grohl's salt-cord are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Take the old west road over the mountains to the Verdant Shore, and show Grohl's salt-cord to Willow-Whisper of the Veridian Keepers.
quests.offer:
Grohl watches Mother Vane tie off the last sack of the woken salt, and doesn't like what he sees at the bottom of the cask. "That's the old salt gone. The pans on the flats are crusting grey, and new salt from them won't bind a cooking pot."

"My grandmother's grandmother got the true salt in the west, past the mountains, on a shore where the forest runs down into the sea. Wood-folk keep it. They let her take it because she asked first." He takes a knotted cord of salt-white hemp from a peg. "Take the old west road, from the fork by Wain's Rest. Show them this. Ask for the one they call Willow-Whisper. And ask first."
quests.complete: She turns the cord over in fingers of woven willow, and the knots loosen at her touch. "An Ash-Walker knot. We have not seen one in three of your lifetimes." Her voice is the sound of wind going through a whole wood at once. "You asked first. That is a beginning. Come into the green, flesh-folk, and let us see what else you are."

steps.text: Take the old west road over the mountains to the Verdant Shore.

objectives.text: Cross the mountains to the Ridge of Long Shadows
objectives.say: The road crests the last ridge and the ash ends as if cut with a knife. Below you the world is green: a thousand greens, from moss so dark it is nearly black to new fern that seems lit from inside, a forest that doesn't know when to stop, rolling west to a line of silver that is the sea. The air doesn't taste of smoke any more.

steps.text: Find Willow-Whisper of the Veridian Keepers and show her Grohl's salt-cord.

objectives.text: Show the salt-cord to Willow-Whisper at Rootfast
objectives.say: "Stop." The word comes out of the trees before she does: a tall, slender shape of living willow and moss, stepping out of a trunk you would have sworn was solid.

quests.title: Salt on the Old Road
quests.canonStatus: CANON company (Sandthrone); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Sandthrone riders are taking the salt carts on the old road west, by Wain's Rest. Clear them and see what the last cart was carrying.
quests.offer: Sefa Brine has stopped counting on her fingers. "The bone-masks steal salt and keep it. These ones sell it." She taps the table. "Sandthrone riders, on the old road past Wain's Rest. My last cart went over in the ditch there and the carter walked home without his boots. Clear the road. Then look in the cart and tell me what they left."
quests.complete: "A Peaks tally-stick, notched for salt." Sefa turns it over and her mouth goes thin. "So the toll-gate buys what its own riders steal from us. Of course it does." She drops the stick in the fire. "You've done the Ash-Walkers a good turn. They'll hear of it."

steps.text: Clear the Sandthrone raiders from the old salt road, south of Wain's Rest.
Search the overturned salt cart.

objectives.say: The salt is gone. Under the tilt, wedged where a man would hide it, a tally-stick notched in the Peaks' way: so many casks, so many crowns, and the toll-gate's mark.

quests.title: What Comes Out of the Wall
quests.canonStatus: CANON creature (Hollow Men); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Something is coming out of the Walled Mouth in the south-east. Grohl wants the wall looked at and the Hollow Men put down.
quests.offer: Grohl is mending a harpoon-line and doesn't stop. "Our grandfathers walled a cave mouth in the south-east. Stone on stone, salt in every joint. We don't say what's in it." He pulls a knot tight. "Grey men are walking out of it now. Go and look at the wall, so you know I'm not a liar. Then put them down. Five."
quests.complete: "Five." Grohl sets the line down for the first time. "And the wall?" You tell him. He is quiet a long while. "Then it isn't keeping anything in any more. It's just a wall." He picks the line up again. "Thank you. Don't go inside."

steps.text: Look at the Walled Mouth.

objectives.say: Salt-white mortar in every joint, and in the middle of the wall a gap a man could walk through, the stones pushed outward from the inside, not pulled down from this side.

steps.text: Put down the Hollow Men out of the Walled Mouth.

quests.title: The Reach-Stones
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (the Pale Things); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Mother Vane wants to know what stands among the Reach-Stones at night, and wants it gone.
quests.offer: Mother Vane pours salt from one hand to the other. "The Reach-Stones, north-east, by the grey. We set them to mark how far the Wasting had come. Every year a little nearer." The salt runs out. "Now there are pale things standing among them at night, as if they were counting the stones too. Go at night. See them. Then send them back to wherever they count from."
quests.complete: "Three." Vane takes a pinch of salt and lets it fall on the back of your hand, which is not a thing she does lightly. "The stones are ours to count. Not theirs." She looks east. "For now."

steps.text: Go to the Reach-Stones after dark.

objectives.text: Stand among the Reach-Stones at night
objectives.say: Three pale shapes stand among the stones, quite still, each facing a stone, the way a clerk faces a ledger.

steps.text: Clear the pale shadows from the Reach-Stones.

quests.title: Cinder-Jaw
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: An old ash hound the Ash-Walkers call Cinder-Jaw hunts alone in the far west, past the Ash Pit. Oska wants it dead.
quests.offer: Oska sets the harpoon down, which she does not do. "There's a hound in the far west, past the Ash Pit. Old. Older than any hound should get. Cinder-Jaw, we call it. It took my brother's harpoon in its mouth once and walked away with it." She picks the harpoon back up. "I made this one for it. You'll have to do, instead."
quests.complete: Oska looks at you a while, then at the harpoon in her hands. "Good." She hangs it on the wall, unused. "That one can stay new."

steps.text: Kill Old Cinder-Jaw, far west past the Ash Pit.

objectives.say: The old hound goes down slowly, and the ash it was made of goes on falling for a while after.

quests.title: The Silent Statue
quests.canonStatus: CANON kind (the faceless statues in the Wasting, world_bible.md); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Grohl wants someone to look at the Silent Statue by the grey and tell Mother Vane what they see.
quests.offer: "There's a statue east of here, at the edge of the grey. No face. It was further away when I was a boy." Grohl says it plainly, as a man says the river is high. "Go and look at it. Then go to the edge of the Wasting and look at that. Then tell Vane. She keeps the count of such things."
quests.complete: Vane listens with her eyes shut. "Nearer," she says. "Always nearer, and never seen walking." She opens them. "Thank you. I'll mark it. One day I'll mark it at the enclave's door, and on that day we go."

steps.text: Look at the Silent Statue.

objectives.say: It has no face, only the smooth stone where a face would be, turned west toward the enclave. There are no footprints in the ash round it. There never are.

steps.text: Stand at the edge of the Wasting.

objectives.text: Stand at the edge of the Wasting
objectives.say: Past the last of the ash the world is not grey so much as not finished: a texture without a picture. It makes no sound. You find you have been holding your breath.

steps.text: Tell Mother Vane what you saw.

quests.title: The Empty Hide
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Ash-Walkers who hunt the Weave-Eaters (book1 ch.20) and the Cult of Ash (book1 ch.10) are canon, and the purple tear is the later House of Ash's sign (series_bible.md), used early as at the shrine; Kesh, the hide and the trail are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Oska's nephew Kesh went up to the Hunters' Knoll to watch for Eaters and has not come down. Go and look for him.
quests.offer:
Oska is carving, and carving badly, which you have not seen her do. "My sister's boy, Kesh. He took his turn on the Hunters' Knoll, out north-west past Cinderfold, watching the plain for Eaters. Three nights." She pares a curl of bone away and frowns at it. "He should have come down yesterday with a story nobody believed. He's a terrible liar. He didn't come down."

"Go up and look. I'd go myself, but if I find what I think I'll find, I'll do something stupid with this harpoon."
quests.progress: "The knoll. North-west, past Cinderfold. Go on."
quests.complete: Oska hears it all with the harpoon across her knees. "Dragged." She turns the harpoon over, and over again. "Then he was alive to be dragged." She stands. "Go and tell Grohl. He'll know where bone-masks take what they drag. I'll be here. Carving."

steps.text: Look for Kesh on the Hunters' Knoll, north-west past Cinderfold.

objectives.text: Search the hide on the Hunters' Knoll
objectives.say: The hide is standing and empty. Kesh's sleeping-fur is still rolled and tied. His harpoon is gone from its pegs, and his salt-cask has been kicked over and the salt trodden into the ash. Round the foot of the knoll the ash is churned with bare prints, and through the middle of them run two long furrows, the kind boot-heels make when someone is dragged. They go south.

steps.text: Follow the furrows south to the salt road.

objectives.text: Follow the furrows to the salt road
objectives.say: The furrows cross the salt road by the wayside shrine at Wain's Rest. Someone has daubed a purple tear on the shrine's stone, fresh enough to come off on your thumb. South of the road the ash is trodden flat by many feet, and the trail is lost among the snags, still going south.

quests.title: What the Pit Keeps
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Cult of Ash and its bone masks (book1 ch.10) and the Ash-Walkers' salt (book1 ch.20) are canon; the pouches, the family knots and the Ash Pit's trophies are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Take the Ash-Walker salt-pouches the cultists at the Ash Pit wear as trophies, and bring them to Oska, who can tell by the knots whose they were.
quests.offer:
Grohl hears you out with his one eye shut. "Dragged south, over the salt road. Then the Ash Pit, in the far south-west." The eye opens. "The bone-masks at the pit don't take prisoners. They take offerings."

"And they keep trophies. Every one of them wears a salt-pouch on his belt, and every pouch was a hunter of ours, lost on the ash these ten years. Bring five home and give them to Oska. Every family ties its own knot, and she knows them all."
quests.progress: "Five pouches. They wear them on the belt, on the left. Like a purse."
quests.complete: "Kesh's." Oska unpicks the knot, which she taught him, and ties it again properly. "Tied this week. So they had him this week." She does not look up. "The Ash-Deacon keeps the pit. Whatever's given to the light down there, he does the giving."

steps.text: Take the salt-pouches from the cultists at the Ash Pit.
Bring the pouches to Oska.

objectives.say: Oska lays the pouches in a row along her anvil and reads the knots with her fingers, one by one, saying each name under her breath. At the fifth she stops.

quests.title: The Ash-Deacon
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Ash-Walker harpoons of petrified leviathan bone (book1 ch.20) and the Cult of Ash (book1 ch.10) are canon; the Ash-Deacon, Kesh and his harpoon are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Bring down the Ash-Deacon at the bottom of the Ash Pit and take back Kesh's harpoon, which would not burn. The Deacon is dangerous alone.
quests.offer:
Oska has stopped carving altogether. "The Ash-Deacon. He kneels at the bottom of the pit, and the rest kneel round him, and whatever's carried down to him gets burned." Her voice is perfectly level. "Kesh had his harpoon with him. My bone, my cord. It won't have burned; the old bone never does. So the Deacon has it still."

"Bring it back to me. And take friends. He's no hedge-preacher: the grey's in him, and his flock will stand for him."
quests.progress: "The old bone doesn't burn. He has it. Go and get it."
quests.complete: "Too old to burn." Oska sets it on the pegs among the harpoons she is making, old grey bone among the new. "His was the first I let him carve himself. Look at that barb. Crooked as the toll road." She picks up her knife, and puts it down again. "Thank you. Go and eat something. I can't."

steps.text: Bring down the Ash-Deacon in the Ash Pit and take back Kesh's harpoon.
steps.say: The Deacon carried Kesh's harpoon as a staff. It lies beside him in the ash, grey bone without a mark of fire on it. Tucked into his belt, where another man would keep a prayer, is a strip of hide written close on both sides.

steps.text: Bring the harpoon home to Oska.

objectives.say: Oska takes it in both hands and runs her thumb down the shaft to the head, where the amber cord should be, and isn't.

quests.title: The Old Sea
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: a beast of the First Era turned to grey stone on the ash plain is canon (book1 ch.20); the Ash-Walkers giving their dead to the old sea and Grohl's cord of names are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The Ash-Walkers give their dead to the old sea. There is nothing of Kesh to give, so go to the Drowned Leviathan after dark and say his name to it, then tell Grohl.
quests.offer:
"We give our dead to the old sea." Oska says it as if you ought to have known. "South, where the leviathan's spine comes up out of the ash. The ash was sea once, and the old ones say it remembers. We carry our dead out at night and lay them along the spine, and by spring the ash has them."

"There's nothing of Kesh to carry. So somebody goes out at night and says his name to it, once, loud, so it knows to look for him. I can't. I'd stay out there. Go after dark. Then tell Grohl; he keeps the names."
quests.complete: Oska listens to the part about the surf and nods once, as if it is what she expected, and as if she is not going to weep in front of a townsman about it. "Good. Then it's looking for him." She takes up her knife. The barbs come out straight.

steps.text: Go to the Drowned Leviathan after dark and say Kesh's name.

objectives.text: Say Kesh's name to the old sea, at night
objectives.say: You stand by the great grey spine with the dark all round you and say his name, once, loud, as Oska asked. The ash does nothing. Then, far down under your feet, so low you feel it in your teeth more than hear it, something like surf.

steps.text: Tell Chieftain Grohl it is done.

objectives.say: Grohl takes down a cord from the peg by the cave mouth, long as a man and heavy with knots, and ties one more at the end of it. He does not ask whose. "Kesh. Oska's sister's boy. Couldn't lie to save himself." He hangs it back up. "Now he's kept."

quests.title: Hollin's Press
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the Last Orchard, Hollin and his press. The grey that unmakes rather than destroys is CANON (world_bible.md).
quests.summary: Thin out the ash hounds denning in the Last Orchard, north of the enclave, and look in at Hollin's press-house to see whether his cider barrels are sound.
quests.offer:
"Hollin kept the Last Orchard, up north along the rim, and paid for his salt in cider. Good cider. Too good. Half my debts started with a cup of it." Sefa Brine doesn't look up from her scales. "When the grey got into his trees he went up the north road to his kin at Oakhaven, with his family and what they could carry. He left the press-barrels sealed and told me they were mine if I fetched them."

"The hounds got there first. They den among his trees now. Thin them out, six or so, and look in at the press-house. If the barrels are sound I'll send a cart. Well. I'll send someone with a cart."
quests.progress: "Six hounds, and the press-house. The house at the end of the orchard lane."
quests.complete: "Grey." Sefa writes something on her tally-board and rubs it out again. "Well, there's my debts settled; nobody's going to drink that." A pause. "Hollin always said his cider would keep forever. He was right, the old liar. It just won't be cider while it does."

steps.text: Thin out the hounds in the Last Orchard and look in at Hollin's press-house.

objectives.say: The press-house door hangs on one hinge. Hollin's barrels are where he left them, sealed with pitch and his mark. You work a bung loose. The cider has gone grey in the barrel: no smell, no sourness, no anything. Not spoiled. Finished.

quests.title: Meat That Does Not Crawl
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: "We have meat that does not crawl" is Grohl's, to the refugees (book1 ch.20); the ash hounds and Sefa's salting are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Bring Sefa Brine five ash-hound flanks to salt down for the enclave's stores.
quests.offer:
"Grohl tells every stray who comes in off the ash that we have meat that does not crawl." Sefa Brine sniffs. "He never says who salts it." She raps an empty cask with her knuckles. "Ash-hound flank. It smells of smoke before it's been near a fire, and salt draws that out. A week in the cask and it's meat. A fortnight and it's very nearly food."

"Bring me five flanks off the hounds, out in the western snags or up at the Last Orchard. Fresh ones. Well. Ones that have stopped moving."
quests.progress: "Five flanks. The cask's waiting, and so is Grohl's boast."
quests.complete: "There. In a fortnight that'll feed the caves for a week, and Grohl can go on telling strays about meat that does not crawl." She wipes her hands on her apron. "You can have the first slice. It'll taste of smoke anyway. Everything here does."

steps.text: Bring Sefa Brine five ash-hound flanks.

objectives.say: Sefa takes the flanks one at a time, sniffs each, and packs them into the cask between handfuls of salt, the way you might lay a fire.

quests.title: What the Tear Is Made Of
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Cult of Ash (book1 ch.10), the purple tear of the later House of Ash (series_bible.md, used early), the Glittering Coast and Port Caelum (world_bible.md) and the Sandthrone toll in the Shattered Peaks are canon; the orchil daub and the road it comes by are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Take four pots of purple daub from the cultists at the tear-marked shrine, so Sefa Brine can tell where the cult gets its paint.
quests.offer:
Sefa Brine has a broken bone-mask on her table and is scratching at its purple tear with a thumbnail. "Grohl burned the litany. I'd sooner know who sells them their paint." She sniffs her thumb. "Nothing on the ash makes purple. Nothing. So it comes from somewhere, and somebody carries it, and somebody gets paid."

"The bone-masks at the shrine carry their daub in little pots, to touch the tears up when the ash wears them off. Bring me four. I'll tell you where it came from by the smell."
quests.progress: "Four pots. They keep them on a thong round the neck, so the daub stays warm and soft."
quests.complete: Sefa unstops a pot, sniffs, and holds it at arm's length. "Orchil. Lichen-purple, scraped off the rocks of the Glittering Coast and steeped in... well. Steeped. You don't want to know in what." She stops it again. "Four crowns a pot at Port Caelum, and dearer every mile. It comes up the toll road with the wool and the iron, and the toll-gate takes its cut like anything else." She sets the pots in a row. "So the Peaks sell the bone-masks their tears. I'll mention it, next time they ask my price for salt."

steps.text: Take pots of tear-daub from the cultists at the tear-marked shrine.

quests.title: Breath on Cold Glass
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Weave-Eaters born of the Weave's frayed threads are canon (book1 ch.20); the Fraying and Vane's measuring of it are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Stand at the lip of the Fraying, south-east behind the Ridge, and thin the Weave-Eaters rising out of it, so Mother Vane knows how fast it is growing.
quests.offer:
Mother Vane draws a line in the ash of the cave floor with one finger, then another beside it, a little to the west. "The Fraying. South-east, behind the Ridge, where the grey licks in. Most of the Eaters on the Rim start there. They rise out of it like breath on cold glass." She draws a third line, further west again. "It's growing. I want to know how fast."

"Go and stand at its lip and look at it. Then thin what's rising out of it. Six. Count them as you go; I'll want the number, not a guess."
quests.progress: "Six, and the lip of it. The number, mind. Not a guess."
quests.complete: "Six, and more rising behind them." Vane rubs out her lines with the heel of her hand. "When I was a girl you could stand on the Ridge and not see it at all." She watches the fire a while. "Don't tell Grohl it's growing. He knows. He just doesn't like to hear it said."

steps.text: Stand at the lip of the Fraying, south-east behind the Ridge.

objectives.text: Stand at the lip of the Fraying
objectives.say: The grey ends in an edge you can't quite look at, like a blade turned toward you. Past it the ash has no grain at all. As you watch, a stir in the nothing becomes a shape, and the shape becomes an Eater, and it turns toward you.

steps.text: Thin the Weave-Eaters rising out of the Fraying.

quests.title: Violet in the Grey
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Void-Seed planted in Oakhaven's water to force a local Wasting, and the Hollow Men, are canon (book1 ch.4); that Cinderfold was seeded the same way, and the grit, are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Put down the Hollow Men of Cinderfold and see whether there is violet grit in what is left of them, as there was violet in Oakhaven's well.
quests.offer:
Mother Vane has been turning your story of Oakhaven over: the black wagon, the ledger, the seed in the well. "Cinderfold went grey in one night. All of it at once, and Sefa's people with it." She keeps her voice low; Sefa's stall is not far off. "The grey doesn't come all at once. Not by itself. It creeps. Ask the Reach-Stones."

"Oakhaven's well had a seed in it, and the seed glowed violet in the dark. Put down the hollows in Cinderfold and look in the grey of them. If there's violet grit in it, bring me five pinches. If there isn't, bring me nothing, and I'll be glad."
quests.progress: "Five pinches. Or none. I'd rather none."
quests.complete: "Seeded." Mother Vane lays a cloth over the bowl the way you would cover a face. "Same as your well. Somebody walked down Cinderfold's lane with a seed in his pocket, and walked home after." She looks across at Sefa's stall. "Not a word to her. Not yet. Let me find the way to say it, if there is one."

steps.text: Put down the Hollow Men of Cinderfold and search the grey of them for violet grit.
Bring the grit to Mother Vane.

objectives.text: Give the grit to Mother Vane
objectives.say: She tips the grit into a bowl of salt. It hisses like fat on a griddle, and the salt round each grain goes grey.

quests.title: Never Seen Walking
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Statues, faceless monoliths in the Wasting (book1/world_bible.md), and the Pale Things as watchers rather than mere monsters (world_bible.md) are canon; this statue, the print and whatever walks it are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Watch the Silent Statue after dark, then tell Mother Vane exactly what you saw.
quests.offer:
"Vane says nearer." Grohl is sharpening the glass spikes of his mace one at a time, which takes a long while. "She says it every year. This year she said it twice." He tries a spike with his thumb. "Nobody's ever seen the thing move. So somebody has to watch it at night, when nobody does. You. You've the least sense of anyone here."

"Go to the Silent Statue after dark and watch it. Then tell Vane exactly what you saw. Not what you think you saw. She'll know the difference."
quests.progress: "After dark. Watch it. Don't touch it."
quests.complete: Grohl stops sharpening. "Something's walking it." He says it over to himself, as if tasting it. "Well. That's worse." He goes back to the spikes. "I'll set a watch on it. Not you. You've had enough of that one."

steps.text: Watch the Silent Statue after dark.

objectives.text: Watch the Silent Statue after dark
objectives.say: For a long while it is only stone. Then the moon comes out from behind the ash-cloud and there is a face on it: not carved, only shadow, as if the stone remembered having one. It is looking at the enclave. At its foot, in the smooth ash, there is a single print, long and narrow, of no foot you know. Only the one.

steps.text: Tell Mother Vane exactly what you saw.

objectives.text: Tell Mother Vane what you saw
objectives.say: Vane hears it with her eyes shut. "One print." She opens them. "Then it isn't walking. Something is walking it."
